strings.d:news:0:
SACRED GOLD PLUS
What's New in 1.3.2 | Current multilingual edition
strings.d:news:1:
YOUR ADVENTURE, WITH MORE CHOICES
Explore Johto and Kanto in an independent continuation of Drayano's Sacred Gold and the original Sacred Gold Plus. Fairy typing, additional Fairy moves and the wider outdoor camera come from the original Plus project. This guide introduces the current English, Italian, French, Spanish and German editions and explains the additions since 1.2.5.
strings.d:news:3: In Options, press SELECT for the Plus settings. Trainer difficulty and wild level scaling can be selected separately; levels stay capped at 100. Plus also controls Pokemon motion in battle, character loading and the Wi-Fi connection slot. Network services depend on your emulator and service provider.
strings.d:news:4: The classic HeartGold camera is built into 52 interiors and caves. Outdoors, the wider Plus view remains. The main Bag pocket offers 252 slots, with extra capacity in other pockets. Consecutive Rare Candy use keeps the party menu open while preserving normal evolution and move-learning prompts.
strings.d:news:5: These camera, Bag, difficulty and motion features were already available in 1.2.5. If you are coming from the original Plus 1.03, the continuation also adds Italian dialogue and interface work, an accented Italian naming keyboard, distributed NPC loading, battle-menu caches, Wi-Fi slot selection and over 200 text corrections. The new field tools below build on that foundation.
strings.d:news:7: Open Guide from the field menu for 467 entries covering evolutions, important items and TMs, special events and training. It uses the current game data and native Pokemon and item names. Browse category lists and linked detail pages with the buttons; L/R moves through lists in groups of five. Returning from a link restores your previous page and position.
strings.d:news:8: The revised Plus settings and Guide use native-style windows, selection frames and contextual help. Apply confirms your Plus edits; cancelling keeps the previous settings. The Shiny page is part of this same settings flow.
strings.d:news:9: Plus settings and Guide distinguish a single direction press from a held direction, using the game's native initial delay and repeat cadence. This corrects overly fast scrolling and a brief press moving more than one item or page.
strings.d:news:10: The existing EV/IV reader remains in the Pokemon summary: L shows EVs, R shows IVs and SELECT returns to normal stats. The field Guide and the summary reader are separate tools. Both work without cheats.
strings.d:news:12: IV consultants in the Violet and Blackthorn PokeMarts use Silver and Gold Caps. Silver changes one IV to 31 or an exact value from 0 to 31; Gold changes all six to 31. These are real IV changes and may affect breeding and Hidden Power. Cancelling, an unchanged value or a refused payment does not consume a Cap.
strings.d:news:13: Silver Caps cost 10,000 after the first Badge; Gold Caps cost 50,000 after the League. Each Johto Badge awards two Silver Caps; each Kanto Badge awards three. The eighth and sixteenth Badges also award a Gold Cap. The first League victory gives four Silver and two Gold; later victories give four Silver and one Gold. The first victory over Red gives three Gold.
strings.d:news:14: Eligible historical one-time rewards can be collected on an existing save; earlier League rematches are not paid retroactively. Full-Bag rewards remain pending instead of being discarded.
strings.d:news:15: At the Route 34 Day Care, quick EV training charges 100 per EV added; reductions and resets are free. Classic permits 252 per stat and 510 overall. Unlimited permits 252 in each stat after a balance warning. Switching to a stricter mode does not silently erase existing EVs: reduce incompatible values explicitly.
strings.d:news:16: Free courses for deposited Pokemon provide one level per two hours and optionally 32 EVs per hour toward a selected target. Choose real time or active playtime. The usual Day Care withdrawal fee still applies. Breeding remains step-based. Course results preserve known moves and are applied on withdrawal; the Day Care Pokegear contact reports projected progress.
strings.d:news:18: The second Plus page offers Classic and Pro shiny profiles independently of difficulty. Classic uses 1/512 for eligible generation. In Pro, the selected target progresses from 1/4096 through 1/2048 and 1/1024 to 1/512 as its completed chain reaches 10, 20 and 40. The improved threshold applies to the next generated encounter. No threshold guarantees a shiny.
strings.d:news:19: Catching or defeating the target advances its chain. An ordinary different species, escape, loss or draw breaks it; excluded encounters suspend it. Changes to mode or target reset the chain and charge; cancelling an edit preserves them. Existing generated Pokemon are not rerolled.
strings.d:news:20: Search chooses a seen species from the area's native encounter pool, respecting available rods, terrain, time, forms and progression. It needs 40 valid steps. Prepare Search in the menu, confirm Apply and return to a free field. A successful Search spends the charge. A normal SAVE retains the mode, target, chain and random state; cold restart resets the charge.
strings.d:news:21: Eggs, gifts, starters, trades, Mystery Gift, roamers, trainer Pokemon, Safari, contests, double encounters and forced events retain their separate native paths. Eligible ordinary static encounters use their base shiny chance without a chain bonus.
strings.d:news:23: From the ordinary field party menu, press R for the native Pokemon storage interface. The shortcut uses the game's PC application and its normal storage operations. Some game contexts prevent the shortcut; follow its in-game feedback and keep the normal save routine.
strings.d:news:24: Portable storage opens the game’s native PC interface from the ordinary field party menu.
strings.d:news:26: The 1.3 species review covers all 493 species and changes selected entries. It affects 67 species: 50 have stat changes, two gain a second ability slot and 29 learnsets receive 32 level/move additions. These categories overlap.
strings.d:news:27: Examples include improved early-game stats for Rattata/Raticate, more physical resilience and Sludge Bomb access for Tentacruel, better pre-Transform survival for Ditto, Technician as a second slot for newly generated Kricketune and Natural Cure as a second slot for newly generated Meganium. Existing Pokemon keep their identity, IVs, EVs, moves and abilities. Affected stats are recalculated through the game's normal loading paths; added level-up moves are also available through the Move Reminder.
strings.d:news:28: Plus difficulty adds nine purposeful move substitutions across seven trainers. Normal retains its original parties. General species and learnset changes apply in both modes. The caught-species Ball is also shown in trainer battles when the Pokedex records the species as caught.
strings.d:news:29: Will-O-Wisp has 85 accuracy. Effective Keen Eye ignores the target's evasion changes while retaining the game's ability-suppression rules. These are selected changes, not a complete later-generation ruleset. The repository contains the full species and trainer comparison.
strings.d:news:31: Keep your current normal save, progress and settings. Before updating, save in-game, fully close the emulator and locate the save it actually uses. Back up that raw save and the installed ROM. Apply one matching patch to a separate file and verify the complete finished-file SHA-256 in the installation PDF.
strings.d:news:32: Test the successor with a separate copy of your save: Continue, inspect progress, Pokemon, Bag including extra slots and Plus settings, SAVE in-game, close fully, cold-start and Continue again. Then replace only the installed ROM, keeping the same language, filename, location and emulator association. Keep your current personal save in its original location; never replace it with the test save.
strings.d:news:33: No new game or settings reset is required. If Continue is missing, stop and correct the save association. Do not load an old emulator savestate after changing the ROM. Keep the backup if returning to an older game, which may not expose extra Bag slots or newer data. This package includes no unverified cheat catalogue; read Cheats/README.txt.
strings.d:news:35: Retail fixes retained from earlier versions: Heavy Ball's neutral 102.4-204.7 kg band was already corrected in Plus 1.1; Hail after Snow Warning was already corrected in Plus 1.03. Fast Ball and Quick Ball follow their separate rules.
strings.d:news:36: Moves and Pokemon: repairs cover Fire Fang/Wonder Guard, Rage/Transform state, transformed-stat reloads, trainer alternate-form stats/abilities, Giratina's party stats after the PC, and AI checks for Dry Skin, Motor Drive, immunities and legal switches.
strings.d:news:37: Field and rewards: targeted fixes address interrupted poisoned-follower jumps, Waterfall facing, six invisible-grass tiles on Routes 43/44, the League guard after viewing GS Cup species, and Kurt/Pryce rewards with full pockets. Other repairs cover GB Sounds after evolution move-learning and playtime/Pokeathlon counters.
strings.d:news:39: Battle and AI: Fairy matchups and Conversion 2, Ghost damage against Dragon/Dark, Iron Ball/Gravity interactions, selected move scoring and a type-check loop that could freeze the return to the move menu.
strings.d:news:40: Pokemon and events: evolution parameters for Mantyke, Feebas, Burmy and Combee; selected fishing records; Mew's movement; Steven's pending reward and Ho-Oh/Lugia scene selectors.
strings.d:news:41: Items, saves and interfaces: the Goldenrod Underground pickup quantity, full-Bag gifts, Plus-settings recovery, extra Bag data protection, story flags that overlapped Friend Roster/Chatot data, and Guide/Options navigation and transitions. Earlier fixes such as Garchomp's Rough Skin, Claydol's Fly and Scizor's Night Slash remain included.

strings.d:news:44: Drayano; mikelan / Mikelan98; NefariousnessNo3436; @JD48096761 and the original contributors. Fairy typing, additional Fairy moves and the wider outdoor camera come from the original Plus project. The five original gameplay PDFs and trainer reference retain their authors' credits. They are historical gameplay references and may describe differences from the current Plus game.
strings.d:news:45: This is an independent fan continuation, not an official handover. AI-assisted tools including Codex support investigation, implementation, translation, testing and documentation. Third-party rights remain with their owners. Gallery images retain their original capture identities. No emulator, BIOS, save or ROM is included.
strings.d:install:0: Sacred Gold Plus {version} - installation and update
strings.d:install:1: This package contains five separate language folders. Open the folder for the language you want to play, then use its Patch and Documents folders. The language folder identifies the output game; the patch manifest identifies the exact starting ROM.
strings.d:install:2: You need your own unmodified HeartGold game file or an explicitly supported earlier Plus version. You do not need to install intermediate hacks first. No ROM, save, BIOS or emulator is included.
strings.d:install:3: Before updating, SAVE inside your current game and fully close the emulator. Check its current settings to locate the raw .sav it actually uses. Make a fresh backup of that save and the installed ROM. Preserve the originals.
strings.d:install:4: Identify the starting file by its complete SHA-256, not its name. On macOS, run shasum -a 256 followed by the file path. On Windows PowerShell, run Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 followed by the file path. Compare the result with the starting-ROM table below.
strings.d:install:5: Choose exactly one patch from this language folder whose source hash matches your file. Apply it to a separate copy using Rom Patcher JS or xdelta3. In Rom Patcher JS, leave Fix ROM checksum disabled. Never apply every patch in sequence.
strings.d:install:6: Check the complete SHA-256 of the finished .nds against the output identity below. A successful patcher message or a matching title alone does not establish the correct file.
strings.d:install:7: Test the new ROM with a separate copy of your raw save: Continue, inspect progress, Pokemon, inventory including expanded Bag slots and Plus settings, SAVE in-game, fully close the emulator, then cold-start and Continue again.
strings.d:install:8: For the actual update, replace only the installed ROM while retaining its language, variant, filename, path and emulator association. Keep your current personal save in its actual location. Never replace it with the test save or an older backup. Confirm its hash is unchanged by the ROM-only replacement.
strings.d:install:9: No new game or settings reset is required. If Continue is missing, stop and correct the save association. Emulator savestates are tied to their original ROM and are not a replacement for a raw save backup. Keep the previous ROM and save backup for rollback.
strings.d:install:10: The translated gameplay guides describe this candidate. Historical author documents are preserved separately in Originals with their original credits and may describe earlier behavior. No unverified cheat catalogue is supplied.
strings.d:label:same_data: All language editions use the same gameplay data. Names and presentation follow the chosen language.
strings.d:label:candidate_note: Generated from the exact candidate identified by the package manifest.
strings.d:label:event_note: Event instructions use the in-game Guide and current source evidence. This document does not certify a complete playthrough of every event.
strings.d:label:credits_note: Sacred Gold by Drayano; the original Plus project and subsequent contributors retain their credits. Original licenses and documents are preserved in the shared reference folders. Translations do not replace those notices.
strings.d:label:cheats_note: No unverified cheat catalogue is included. Codes must match the exact ROM revision. Updating a ROM can invalidate older cheats.
strings.d:label:language_selector: Choose your game language, then open its installation guide. Use only the patch matching your starting ROM hash.
strings.d:label:new_game_fix: The first conversation with Mom no longer requests an SDK reset on a valid empty New Game event bank.
strings.d:label:new_languages: French, Spanish and German join English and Italian. Official unchanged retail text is reused; Sacred Gold and Plus additions, interfaces and manuals are localized separately.
strings.d:label:encounter_note: The ordinary tables list walking by time of day, Surf, Rock Smash, rods, swarms and radio replacements. Headbutt, the Bug-Catching Contest and the Safari Zone use separate engines and are listed separately. Map #ID is the native map ID; the # column is the encounter slot. % is the native per-slot selection weight. Radio and swarm rows identify replacement slots, not additional independent encounters.
strings.d:label:headbutt_note: Headbutt tables list common, rare and secret tree groups. The actual group depends on the tree and the Trainer ID; a listed species is not available at every tree.
strings.d:label:contest_note: Bug-Catching Contest set 0 applies before the National Pokédex. After the National Pokédex, sets 1, 2 and 3 apply on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday respectively.
strings.d:label:safari_note: Safari thresholds are native object points, including boosts from object age. Bonus replacements are applied in their stored order. The configured areas and objects determine the encounters; a table row is not a guarantee for every setup.
strings.p:r2:install:1: This main package has five language folders. Choose your game language. Its Patch folder contains one clean-ROM patch; the installation and What's New PDFs are directly in the language folder. The seven shared English guides, updated for 1.3.2, are in Originals.
strings.p:r2:install:2: Use your own unmodified HeartGold ROM in the same language as the chosen folder (US English for EN). The separate optional updater archive provides all 150 recognized historical source-to-language routes. It is only needed if you want to patch a supported older ROM directly. No intermediate installation is required. No ROM, save, BIOS or emulator is included.
strings.p:r2:install:5: Apply the single patch in this language folder's Patch folder to the matching clean ROM, writing a separate file. Use Rom Patcher JS or xdelta3. In Rom Patcher JS, leave Fix ROM checksum disabled. If using the separate optional updater archive, select exactly one route by its complete source SHA-256. Never apply patches in sequence.
strings.p:r2:install:10: English guides updated for 1.3.2: Originals contains exactly seven shared gameplay PDFs, including one Game Guide. They describe the current game and retain contributor credits. These guides are English in all five editions; installation and What's New are localized. Read the language folder's Cheats/README.txt before using codes.

strings.p:r2:label:updater_intro: Optional direct updater routes for Sacred Gold Plus 1.3.2. This language folder contains 30 alternative patches for recognized starting ROMs. Identify your source by its complete SHA-256 in the table, then apply exactly one matching patch to a separate output file. The folder identifies the output language. Never apply the patches in sequence. In Rom Patcher JS, leave Fix ROM checksum disabled. Verify the full output SHA-256 below. Before updating an existing installation, back up its active raw save and installed ROM, and follow the localized installation PDF in the main package for Continue, in-game SAVE, cold restart and ROM-only replacement while retaining the current save and filename/path.
strings.p:r2:walk:h2: 2. Where do I find my SHA-256?
strings.p:r2:walk:h4: 4. Apply the patch in your browser
strings.p:r2:walk:h5: 5. Check the result, then first play
strings.p:r2:walk:download: Open the official release page below. Under Assets download Sacred-Gold-Plus-1.3.2-{package_revision}-Multilingual.zip. Automatic Source code downloads are for developers. Optional-Updaters is a separate, optional ZIP for recognized older ROMs. The main ZIP has one clean-ROM patch per language.
strings.p:r2:walk:extract: Windows: right-click the ZIP, choose Extract All, then Extract. Mac: double-click the ZIP in Finder; if Safari already extracted it, open that folder. Open the extracted folder, not the ZIP preview. Choose your game-language folder: its two PDFs are directly inside and the patch is in Patch.
strings.p:r2:walk:files: The four files: .nds = your game ROM; .xdelta = a patch that cannot be played; .sav = your progress; .zip = a compressed container. Extract your own .nds first if archived. Never select a ZIP, patch or save as the ROM. Use a backup from your own HeartGold cartridge; no ROM is supplied.
strings.p:r2:walk:backup: Compare each backup’s SHA-256 with its original to verify the copy. Record the active ROM/save names, paths and emulator association. Keep originals and backups untouched. The hash methods in step 2 also work for these files.
strings.p:r2:walk:sha_what: SHA-256 is a 64-character fingerprint calculated from your file contents. It is not printed on the cartridge or determined by the filename. Renaming the file does not change it. Choose ONE method below; each reads the file without changing it.
strings.p:r2:walk:sha_where: YOUR hash: calculate it from the extracted starting .nds. EXPECTED starting hash: Reference A in step 3. EXPECTED finished hash: Reference B in step 5. Before and after should differ. The release SHA256SUMS checks downloaded ZIPs, not your ROM. Use Ctrl+F (Windows) or Command+F (Mac) in this PDF to find a complete hash.
strings.p:r2:walk:browser: Open the link below; check the heading SHA256 File Checksum. In Settings use Input Type = File and Output Encoding = Hex; leave HMAC disabled. Click the Input chooser or drag your .nds into Input. Wait for Output; click Hash if needed, then Copy. The selected local file is processed in the browser without uploading it. Copy all 64 characters.
strings.p:r2:walk:mac: Press Command+Space, type Terminal and open it. Type shasum -a 256 followed by a space. Drag the .nds from Finder into Terminal to insert its full path, then press Return. Copy the first 64 characters of the result, not the filename after them. Example:
strings.p:r2:walk:windows: Right-click the .nds and choose Copy as path (hold Shift on some versions). Open Windows PowerShell from Start. Replace the example path below with the copied path: remove outer double quotes and keep the single quotes shown. Double an apostrophe inside a filename. Press Enter and copy the 64-character result.
strings.p:r2:walk:hash_warn: Use SHA-256, not CRC32, MD5 or SHA-1. Rom Patcher JS displays those other hashes; they do not match this PDF’s SHA-256. Uppercase/lowercase hexadecimal letters are equivalent. Compare all 64 characters, not just the beginning or end.
strings.p:r2:walk:choose: Match the full starting SHA-256 below and use exactly this patch path. Every patch goes directly to 1.3.2; never apply patches in sequence. For a supported older ROM, the separate optional updater archive and README-Updater.txt list direct routes by full source hash.
strings.p:r2:walk:stop: No match? Stop. An English European ROM is not automatically the US ROM. SoulSilver, other revisions and trimmed or edited files differ. Renaming, guessing a patch or bypassing validation will not fix it. If your ROM already matches Reference B, you already have this exact 1.3.2 game.
strings.p:r2:walk:apply_intro: Open the official Rom Patcher JS link below. No program installation is needed on Windows or Mac. Stay in Apply patch mode and leave Creator mode off.
strings.p:r2:walk:select:
a. Beside ROM file select the starting .nds whose SHA-256 you checked. Wait for it to load.
b. Beside Patch file choose the ONE .xdelta from Reference A. Do not select a folder, PDF, manifest.json or your .sav.
strings.p:r2:walk:settings: c. Open Settings; leave Fix ROM checksum disabled. The image shows its box unchecked. Close Settings by clicking outside. Do not add/remove headers or bypass validation.
strings.p:r2:walk:save_output: d. Click Apply patch and wait for a NEW .nds download. Check the browser Downloads list; its name may contain (patched) or follow Use patch name for output. Save a separate file and keep .nds. The name in step 5 is suggested; the full hash decides. Do not replace the installed game yet. Never select or overwrite a .sav.
strings.p:r2:walk:capture: Real Rom Patcher JS v3.5 captures, 27 October 2026. No ROM loaded. The chooser follows the computer language; fields are ROM file and Patch file. These program screenshots are not proof of a finished ROM.
strings.p:r2:walk:verify: Repeat a SHA-256 method from step 2 for the NEW downloaded .nds. Compare the entire result with Reference B below. A success message, filename or title screen alone is insufficient. If it differs, do not install the file; see step 7. The output name below is for the new file before updating an existing installation.
strings.p:r2:walk:firstplay: First installation: open your Nintendo DS emulator, choose Open/Load ROM and select the verified .nds. ZIP and .xdelta cannot be played. Follow the emulator’s setup instructions; no emulator or BIOS is included. Cheats are optional, not required to install or play. Read Cheats/README.txt before using them.
strings.p:r2:walk:copy: Keep the emulator closed. Put the verified new ROM in a temporary test location with a SEPARATE COPY of your current raw save. Confirm the emulator reads that copy. If pairing uses filenames, use the matching test names below. For app-managed saves use supported import/export in the isolated test location. Renaming .dsv to .sav does not convert it. Never import a blank or test save over the personal save.
strings.p:r2:walk:update_note: Only AFTER the copied-save check passes, rename the verified successor to the CURRENT installed ROM filename when replacing it at its original path. Open the existing game entry and Continue. Keep the backups for rollback; the test copy is temporary, not a second normal installation.
strings.p:r2:walk:trouble:
No source match: check the extracted .nds, not ZIP or .sav; check whether it already matches Reference B. Otherwise use your matching clean cartridge backup or an explicitly recognized optional route.
Checksum mismatch or source too short: recheck Reference A and exact patch path. Keep validation enabled; retry untouched files in a current desktop browser.
Wrong output hash: check the NEW file, correct language patch, Fix ROM checksum off and no second patch. Re-extract the official ZIP and retry.
strings.p:r2:walk:help: Need help? Use the issue link below. Include source SHA-256, ZIP name, patch path, patcher/browser and exact error. Do not upload a ROM or personal save.
strings.p:r2:walk:offline: The browser is sufficient for beginners. xdelta3 is an offline alternative from the official project below. Mac with Homebrew already installed: brew install xdelta. Windows: use a compatible executable from official releases. Open Terminal/PowerShell in this language folder. Replace source.nds with your checked path; quote paths with spaces. The Windows executable name may differ. Create a NEW output and verify it with step 5.
